messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] help!
parts:
On 3/4/13 6:08 PM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
> Is there ever a situation in Stan where '=' means anything besides "I
> meant to type <-" (or more rarely "I meant to type ==")?

There's the lower and upper bounds.

real<lower=12,upper=27> x;

Maybe those should've been "<-", as in:

real<lower<-12, upper<-27>

But that just looks really really ugly, and R used
"=" for properties, and we followed R syntax.

> Should be
> pretty easy to catch, if not.

Conceptually, yes it's easy. But what it means in practice is
that we have to write a separate parser rule that looks like
an assignment, but with an "=" in place of the '<-', then throw an error when
it matches. Not too hard. But when we add more rules, we
immediately break windows and have to break our parser into
more bits, ...

> (We could even translate it to <- like R
> does, but I don't want to start a heated discussion on that topic.)

We've had it already and decided on just "<-".

FWIW, I liked "=" instead of "<-" and "double" instead
of "real" so that I don't have such a jarring context switch
going back and forth with C++. But I also would rather just
have a single symbol.

- Bob
